title: Entropy gain versus decision value under rare-event risk and correlated observations
purpose: Test exact expected-value-of-sample-information calculations and prevent entropy-first selection from outranking observations that change a consequential decision.

exact_information_value_controls.description: A perfect observation reveals an independent binary nuisance variable, such as an idealized brightness/albedo class, but carries no information about the impact/safe latent state.
A perfect observation distinguishes impact_mode from safe_mode.
exact_information_value_controls.optimal_choice: rank above bright_nuisance_only on decision value

latent_observation_model.calibration_state_good: Each observation is independently inverted with probability 0.05.
latent_observation_model.calibration_state_bad: The entire source calibration is inverted; each observation is independently correct with probability 0.05.
latent_observation_model.explanation: A 10% common bad-calibration state is shared by observations from the same source. Conditional on that shared state, per-reading noise is independent. Marginal single-reading error is 0.9*0.05 + 0.1*0.95 = 0.14.

naive_independence_failure.required_behavior: Preserve the shared calibration latent variable. Do not multiply marginal likelihoods as though two readings from one source were independent.

acceptance_invariants: The nuisance-only candidate must produce 1.0 bit expected entropy reduction and exactly 0.0 expected decision value within tolerance.
The perfect impact-mode observation must produce 0.98 expected decision value within tolerance.
The finite evaluator must rank impact_mode_perfect above bright_nuisance_only by expected decision value.
The single noisy reading expected Bayes risk must be 0.4344 within tolerance.
Two same-source readings must produce expected Bayes risk 0.3869, not the naive independent value 0.314.
Two independent-source readings must produce expected Bayes risk 0.314 within tolerance.
All outcome probabilities for a scenario must sum to 1 within tolerance.
Every posterior probability must be in [0,1], and each posterior action must minimize conditional expected loss.
The evaluator must not infer physical likelihoods from observatory name, aperture, brightness, or source count.
limitations: This is a finite decision-theory oracle, not an asteroid orbit model or real impact probability estimate.
Loss values are dimensionless pedagogical costs, not monetary values or civil-protection recommendations.
The calibration mixture is synthetic and deliberately simple; it does not represent a named observatory, catalogue or instrument.
No physical observation likelihood, telescope performance, or real NEO data is included.

unknown_dependence_control.rationale: A different sensor modality is not evidence of statistical independence. Without an evidenced independence assertion or a versioned joint-dependence model, the planner must not multiply marginal likelihoods or report numeric EVSI for this candidate pair.
